source: Only the freshly supplied 3d-lab(2).zip; no cApp owner or native runtime changes.
verified: Real surface/vertex/edge tracking, visible brush radius, keyboard focus guards and orthographic cut projection
Concave outline separation with interpolated attributes; cuts before and after shelling; closed Float32 output topology
57,120-triangle synthetic mesh split and independent topology checks
Point correction including first-point drag, click-to-close and pending-outline navigation guard
Actual Move handle dragging, baking, undo and interrupted-drag rollback
Direct brush edits, one-stroke undo and cancelled-stroke restoration
Object transforms, duplication, filtering, locks and hidden-object persistence through GLB save/reopen
Native and fallback fullscreen with accessible tool and object panels
Manual and real automatic WebGL context restoration retaining edits
Unchanged original draft bytes and retained working geometry after save failure
Existing generation workflow and full-detail multi-megabyte saves using controlled engine replies
Desktop/mobile layouts and no unexpected browser requests or uncaught errors
limitations: Installed Windows WebView2 and RTX 4070 behaviour remain unverified here.
Neural inference, Windows packaging and new native runtimes were not exercised in this update.
Outlines are fixed orthographic projections, not geodesic paths; wall depth must reach the intended inner skin.
A cut acts on up to 350,000 source triangles, with 3–64 simple points; ambiguous or invalid topology is rejected without replacing the working scene.
Shell offsets can locally thin or intersect at concave folds; inspect the interior before production use.
Glass is a transparent material preset, not optical refraction; reference projection is not generated unseen texturing.
Other GLB viewers can show hidden objects retained in full-scene exports because Builder visibility uses metadata.
Automatic compartment layout, full AI texturing, Shape Studio UI, rigging and external production writes remain future work.
